angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 294,420 km at 36.05 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 27.7400 +/- 0.0125 mas (same row, RUWE 1.23): 36.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.4232 +/- 0.0077 solar radii from Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1266 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..292G/abstract): 294,420 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.437 +/- 0.021 solar masses from Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1266 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..292G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3563 +/- 77 K from Greklek-McKeon et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1266 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..292G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
